revision_summary: No fabricated quotes were found — all quotes check out against the transcript. However, three issues warrant a targeted revision: (1) Schema misuse — Stage 3 applies bill_collection.alternative_paths.elderly_low_tech_protocol (twice, at 01:41-02:07 and 03:33) and shopping_customer_protocol (at 02:07) to a friction pattern that doesn't match either trigger condition. The actual friction is a third party (customer's wife) navigating a billing app on the customer's behalf — not an elderly/low-tech customer struggling with their own phone, and not a customer who is mobile/away-from-home. Revise these references to cite the general bill_collection.alternative_paths time_budget principle (pivot within 2 minutes) rather than mismatched named protocols. (2) The 04:04 'micro_trade' classification for the texted phone number overstates confidence in a personal-phone-number privacy exposure the transcript doesn't establish — the detection_signal in the schema requires explicit personal-line framing, which isn't present here. Soften this to an open question rather than a schema-anchored finding. (3) Missed moments — add positive credit-threshold compliance (01:24, rep states 670 matching schema exactly, notable given known drift in other calls), the correctly-executed scope-discipline escape hatch at 00:29 (rep redirects the customer's estimate request to the specialist appointment immediately, per coaching_philosophy.setter_scope_discipline), and the unprobed roof-age signal at 01:18 ('100 years old' section) which borders on both a DQ condition and a cross-sell opportunity and was never explored by the rep. These are concrete, evidence-based additions a manager would want in the brief. Trajectory shape label 'stagnant' should also be reconsidered/clarified against the fact that the call still closes with a clean booked time — distinguish flat call energy from achieved outcome rather than conflating them under one shape term.
